newsitem.title: FRANCE: Credit National up, broker issues buy advice.
newsitem.headline: Credit National up, broker issues buy advice.

text.p: Credit National shares rose sharply on Monday and fund managers said brokerage Cheuvreux de Virieu had switched its recommendation on the stock from "sell" to "buy".
The share, which has recently been sliding amid speculation that the group could suffer a downgrading by ratings agencies, was up 3.93 percent at 251.0 francs at 1435 GMT.
In a flurry of activity around that time the stock soared, and was up 5.8 percent at 1444 GMT at 255.5 francs.
The fund managers said Cheuvreux de Virieu had a target for the stock of 300 francs.

The broker underlined that the integration of the BFCE bank which it bought last year was going well and that return on shareholder funds would be around six percent in 1998, even on the basis of a more pessimistic appraisal than that given by the banking group itself, they said.
They said the brokerage also said any downgrading by rating agencies would only have a weak impact on resultd and that the share was considerable undervalued.
U.S. investment bank Morgan Stanley switched its recommendation of the stock to "strong buy" and has a target of 400 francs for the stock.
